bc2ed7049b: In creating the mural with spray paint for Boombox Englewood, Matt Sansing has depicted a silhouette of a different Chicago skyline, featuring elements within the surrounding blocks in Englewood. This location is one of four Boombox installations across the city managed by Latent Design. This project was realized in partnership with the People Plazas program of the Chicago Department of Transportation’s Make Way for People initiative, and the Department of Planning and Development’s Retail Thrive Zone program.
d778abbcdb: This mural’s positive symbolism, coupled with the strong use of primary colors, intends to bring a reflective energy to the location as a reminder to balance our mind, matter, and soul.
264a7daabb: Mural on exterior ally wall of Lincoln Hall.
74b2c22f1b: The south wall, “Baseball Rules” is based on a movie quote, “There is only three rules in baseball: you throw the ball, you hit the ball, you catch the ball” with images of Jack McDonald pitching, Frank Thomas hitting and Carleton Fisk, and Dwayne Wise.
c8af96ce5b: three pink coneflowers sprout happily from a bed of grass with a monarch butterfly delicately resting on one of the flowers
92c185049b: 2008. Artist Rahmann Statik. This acrylic and spray paint mural spans the 47th and Lake Park viaduct in Hyde Park. It was created to show an evolution of community, color, and nature.

(Photo Credit: Sandra Steinbrecher) Marina Zumi is most associated with the early street art scene and her work with one of the formative groups “Expression Sessions” in Buenos Aires. Zumi came to street art from a fashion design background which has contributed to the development of a unique style that is colorful and feminine.

While working on this project Zumi stated, “My motivation comes in my daily life. I try to reflect human behavior through natural and animal scenes” – as quoted in Sandra Steinbrecher’s Wabash Arts Corridor / Big Walls / 2016
1d71fde91b: Created in the summer of 2016, this spray painted mural was a collaboration with students and lead Artist GLO.
a5750ce89b: A sprawling mural in Back of the Yards is all about the production of food, its images paying tribute to the meatpacking history of the area and to the building’s current incarnation as the center of an urban farm and food production incubator.
